COMMON.NO_RESULTS: No results matched the applied filters

ERRORS.TITLE: Could not read the hub
ERRORS.NETWORK: No response from the hub. Check that the backend is up and that VITE_API_BASE_URL points to it.
ERRORS.NOT_FOUND: The hub replied that this resource does not exist.
ERRORS.FORBIDDEN: The hub rejected the read for lack of authorization.
ERRORS.SERVER: The hub replied with an internal error.
ERRORS.UNKNOWN: The hub replied with something this client cannot interpret.

ENV_EMPTY.TITLE: No service reports in {{env}}
ENV_EMPTY.BODY: There are no manifests or traffic batches in this environment. The ecosystem is not empty: the hub runtime is simply not enabled here. Turn it on in each service's {{env}} settings.

SERVICES.TITLE: Services
SERVICES.SUMMARY: {{instrumented}} instrumented services · {{uninstrumented}} uninstrumented hosts detected · environment {{env}}
SERVICES.UNINSTRUMENTED_HINT: Hosts detected because someone calls them, but that no service claims. This is the adoption backlog.
SERVICES.UNINSTRUMENTED_EMPTY: Every observed host has an owner in this environment.

HEALTH.TIP_OK: ok — it reports and the report is complete. Last batch {{last}}. Action: none.
HEALTH.TIP_INCOMPLETE: incomplete — what you see understates real traffic. Action: raise MAX_KEYS or review the service's sampling.
HEALTH.TIP_NO_REPORTING: not reporting — there is a recent manifest but no batches since {{last}}. Action: runtime off or flush thread down.
HEALTH.TIP_NO_DATA: no data — the hub has no health row for this service in this environment.
HEALTH.FOOTNOTE: Health is shown where the data is used: this panel opens from any coloured dot or warning band.
HEALTH.ACTION_OK: None. The service reports and the report is complete.
HEALTH.ACTION_NO_REPORTING: The runtime is off or the flush thread died. Check the service process: if there is a recent manifest but no batches, the catalogue still publishes at boot and the traffic report does not.
HEALTH.ACTION_DROPPED: Raise MAX_KEYS: the buffer saturated and dropped {{dropped}} events before sending them. While this holds, every volume from this service is a floor.
HEALTH.ACTION_SAMPLING: Review settings: sampling sits at {{rate}} % in this environment. It helps under load, but it hides low-traffic dependencies.
HEALTH.ACTION_NO_DATA: The hub has received neither manifest nor batches from this service in this environment. Check that the runtime is enabled and that the token matches the environment.
HEALTH.AFFECTS_OK: Nothing. This service's figures can be read as they are.
HEALTH.AFFECTS_NO_REPORTING: Every {{name}} view and any dependency list it appears in. A “no consumers” that depends on {{slug}} is evidence of nothing.
HEALTH.AFFECTS_INCOMPLETE: {{name}}'s volumes and the low-traffic dependencies coming out of it.
HEALTH.WARN_DETAIL_DROPPED: {{dropped}} events dropped in 24 h: the volumes in this list are a floor, and low-traffic dependencies may be missing.
HEALTH.WARN_DETAIL_SAMPLING: Sampled at {{rate}} % in {{env}}: the volumes in this list are a floor, and low-traffic dependencies may be missing.
HEALTH.WARN_DETAIL_NO_REPORTING: What you see is incomplete: any new consumer of {{name}} would be invisible.

SERVICE.WARN_NO_REPORTING: {{name}} has not reported since {{last}}. There is a recent manifest, so the endpoint catalogue is valid, but every traffic figure and every dependency on this page is incomplete. A “no consumers” here means nothing yet.
SERVICE.WARN_DROPPED: Incomplete report: {{dropped}} events dropped in 24 h (MAX_KEYS saturated). The volumes you see are a floor, not the total.
SERVICE.WARN_SAMPLING: Report sampled at {{rate}} % in {{env}}. Volumes are estimates; low-traffic dependencies may not appear.
SERVICE.WARN_NO_DATA: The hub has no health row for this service in {{env}}. Everything here comes from the catalogue, not from traffic.
SERVICE.DEPS_FOOTNOTE: This is the coarse level. Endpoint-by-endpoint detail lives on each endpoint page.
SERVICE.NO_INCOMING: No instrumented service calls {{slug}} in this window.
SERVICE.NO_OUTGOING: {{slug}} does not call any instrumented service in this window.

ENDPOINTS.COUNT_LABEL: {{visible}} endpoints visible out of {{total}} in the catalogue · sorted by {{sort}}
ENDPOINTS.NONE_MATCH_HINT: Retired ones are hidden: turn on “include retired” if you are after an old one.
ENDPOINTS.TIP_RETIRED_HOT: Retired on {{date}} and still receiving {{calls}} calls from {{consumers}} consumers. Someone is going to break.
ENDPOINTS.TIP_DEPRECATED: Marked deprecated in the spec. Still responding.
ENDPOINTS.TIP_UNDOCUMENTED: No description and no use case: invisible to semantic search.
ENDPOINTS.TIP_NO_CONSUMERS: No known consumers — it may mean nobody calls it, or that nobody reports

ENDPOINT.NOT_FOUND_BODY: That id is not in the current catalogue. It may have been retired, or the manifest may be stale.
ENDPOINT.NOT_IN_ENV_BODY: Service {{service}} does not report this endpoint in {{env}}; the catalogue has it in {{origin}}. It may exist in the code and simply not report: what is missing is the manifest, not necessarily the endpoint.
ENDPOINT.NO_DOCS_BODY: Without docs, semantic search cannot find it: nobody will know it exists and someone will write a duplicate. Writing it is the highest-return thing you can do with this endpoint today.
ENDPOINT.NO_DOCS_HINT: registry_dump picks it up on the next deploy; it shows up here without touching the hub.
ENDPOINT.CONTRACT_NO_PARAMS: The OpenAPI spec declares no parameters for this operation.
ENDPOINT.CONTRACT_NO_BODY: The OpenAPI spec declares no requestBody for this operation.
ENDPOINT.CONTRACT_NO_RESPONSES: The OpenAPI spec declares no responses for this operation.
ENDPOINT.CONTRACT_EMPTY: The manifest carried no schema for this endpoint. What is missing is the service spec, not the hub.
ENDPOINT.INCOMING_HINT: who breaks if I change it
ENDPOINT.OUTGOING_HINT: what it calls when it runs
ENDPOINT.NO_INCOMING_BASE: No instrumented endpoint or task called this path in the last {{days}} days. Two possible readings, and they are not the same: nobody uses it, or whoever uses it does not report.
ENDPOINT.NO_INCOMING_UNRELIABLE: There are {{count}} services reporting incomplete or down right now ({{services}}): check their health before concluding it is safe to change.
ENDPOINT.NO_INCOMING_RELIABLE: Every service in the environment reports complete, so this is evidence that nobody calls it — but only within what is instrumented.
ENDPOINT.NO_OUTGOING_BODY: This endpoint's x-registry block does not declare what it calls. The hub observes inbound traffic per endpoint: outbound is declared in the manifest or it does not exist here.
ENDPOINT.DECLARED_ONLY_HINT: they said they depend on this and their traffic never showed up
ENDPOINT.GRAPH_HINT: endpoint to endpoint, this endpoint as the root
ENDPOINT.GRAPH_DENSE: At this depth the graph brings {{count}} nodes and starts to be a tangle. Raise the minimum volume and keep the routes that actually move traffic.
ENDPOINT.GRAPH_EMPTY: There is no inbound traffic to draw with these filters.

SEARCH.PLACEHOLDER: method, path, summary, tag or service…
SEARCH.HINT: Type to search by path, summary or tag. Search is hybrid: semantic and literal.
SEARCH.EMPTY_BODY: It may exist undocumented: semantic search only sees what has a summary or a description.
SEARCH.FOOTER: environment {{env}} — results never mix across environments

STATES.TITLE: Explicit states
STATES.SUBTITLE: With two or three instrumented services at the start, these are not edge cases: they are most of what you will see.
STATES.CARD_1_WHY: Visually identical to “nobody uses it”. It has to say whether that is because nobody reports or because nobody called.
STATES.CARD_1_DEMO_BODY: No instrumented endpoint or task called this path in the window. If a service is not reporting, check its health before concluding it is safe to change.
STATES.CARD_1_CTA: See services that do not report
STATES.CARD_2_WHY: The most valuable alert in the system: the contract is gone and someone keeps calling it.
STATES.CARD_2_DEMO_BODY: The path is marked retired and traffic did not stop. Warn the owning team before shutting the route down.
STATES.CARD_3_WHY: A warning band above the content in every one of its views, not a footnote.
STATES.CARD_3_DEMO_TITLE: This service has not reported in days
STATES.CARD_3_DEMO_BODY: There is a recent manifest, so the catalogue is valid; traffic and dependencies are not. Runtime off or flush thread down.
STATES.CARD_4_WHY: The gap has to push you to write it, with the concrete path in the repo — it is the lever of semantic search.
STATES.CARD_4_DEMO_BODY: Without docs nobody finds it and someone will write a duplicate. It is written in the service view's docstring.
STATES.CARD_5_WHY: Do not draw the tangle: offer to raise the minimum volume.
STATES.CARD_5_DEMO_BODY: At this depth the graph stops being legible. Keep the routes that move real traffic.
STATES.CARD_6_WHY: Normal in staging at the start. It is not an error, it is pending configuration.
STATES.CARD_6_DEMO_BODY: There are no manifests or batches. The hub runtime is not enabled in this environment:

SYSTEM.TITLE: System
SYSTEM.SUBTITLE: Defined once, used across the four screens. Switch the theme with the top-bar toggle to see the other mode.
SYSTEM.TYPE_SAMPLE_BODY: 11/400 body and tables · 12/500 badges · 11/600 table headers
SYSTEM.TYPE_SAMPLE_CODE: Technical data uses Verdana with open tracking, not a monospaced font
SYSTEM.USE_DELETE: removal · shares its tone with error
SYSTEM.COMP_METHOD_RULE: Fixed colour per verb, derived from the palette's semantics. The same badge in table, graph and search.
SYSTEM.COMP_ROW_RULE: Method, path, summary, consumers. Reused in the service page, search and dependencies.
SYSTEM.COMP_HEALTH_RULE: Coloured dot, label and hover explanation. Four states, four different actions.
SYSTEM.COMP_SERVICE_RULE: Square with the initial tinted per service, name and link. The tint comes from the palette, it is not free colour.
SYSTEM.COMP_VOLUME_RULE: Compact in the cell, exact on hover and an estimate notice when sampling happened.
SYSTEM.COMP_STALE_RULE: The same in lists, tables and graph edges: dimmed, labelled and with a visible date.
